description:
Viral Ninja Creami Peach "Ice Cream" and "Sorbet"

Now depending on where you look, this recipe started as a Sorbet release on TikTok then got rereleased as an Ice Cream recipe. Today i'm looking at this as the ice cream variation instead of sorbet but ultimately it's TERRIBLE as either sorbet or ice cream and it was just released as the same thing...a single can of peaches FFS!

In this video, I’ll walk you through how to make it better step by step. I'll talk about what you need to look at regrading recipe adjustments to make something in to a decent ice cream. In later videos, i'll show you how to change recipes in to amazing sorbets and gelato too.


Ingredients:
1 Whole can of sliced Peaches (DelMonte brand used here sugar content 8g/167ml)
70g Allulose 
100g Whipping  Cream (33-36% fat) (Double Cream can also be used, it'll just be creamier!)
25g inulin NEEDED FOR SOLIDS
1g Xanthan


All the ingredietns are important, like a say in the video. They're chosen for specific reasons, if you miss one of sub it out without understnding why, the result will be sub-par. 


👉 If you enjoyed this video, don’t forget to like, comment, and subscribe for more viral Ninja Creami recipes, ice cream hacks, and frozen treat experiments!

⸻

Question:  What can a Ninja creami make that cannot be made in a compressor churn ice cream machine? 

Chat GPT Answer:

Great question — and it gets right to the heart of why the Ninja Creami isn’t just a “cheap churner.” A compressor churn ice cream machine (like your Breville/Sage BCI600) and the Ninja Creami work on very different principles:

⸻

🔄 Process Differences
	•	Compressor churn: Cools and churns at the same time. Base must be fluid (custard, cream mix, sorbet base). Freezes gradually while incorporating air → a continuous, creamy frozen dessert.
	•	Ninja Creami: Base is frozen solid first. Later, the spinning blade drills into the block, shaving it into a pseudo-churned texture. You can respin or “mix-in” after the fact.

⸻

✅ Things a Ninja Creami Can Do That a Churn Cannot
	1.	Refreeze & Re-spin
	•	You can make a pint, scoop some out, refreeze, and spin again days later.
	•	A compressor churn can’t take a partially frozen base and “re-churn” it back to fresh texture.
	2.	Single-serve customization
	•	Different pints can be prepared (low-sugar, high-protein, boozy, savory, etc.), stored in the freezer, and spun one at a time.
	•	A churn forces you to make a batch and eat/store it immediately.
	3.	Post-spin Mix-ins
	•	Creami lets you core out the middle of a frozen pint, add chocolate chunks, bacon bits, nut butters, syrups, etc., and reincorporate with a spin.
	•	Compressor churners require you to add mix-ins only while the machine is running, limiting flexibility.
	4.	Turning non-traditional liquids into frozen desserts
	•	Protein shakes, electrolyte drinks, flavored waters, bone broth, or even coffee can be frozen solid and spun.
	•	A churn can’t start from something as watery or low-fat without heavy stabilizers — it will freeze hard, not creamy.
	5.	“Rescue” icy or failed bases
	•	If a frozen pint comes out icy, you just hit “Respin” and it becomes smoother.
	•	In a churn, if your base isn’t balanced (wrong sugar/fat ratio), you can’t really fix it post-churn.
	6.	Higher tolerance for alcohol and sugar extremes
	•	Very boozy or very low-sugar bases, which would stay slushy or rock-hard in a churn, can still be shaved smooth by the Creami.
	•	That’s why people make things like frozen cocktails in the Creami.

⸻

⚠️ Things a Compressor Churn Does Better
	•	Superior overrun control (air incorporation) → more consistent texture, especially for classic dairy ice creams.
	•	Natural emulsion development during freeze → better mouthfeel for custards.
	•	Larger batch sizes and continuous production.
	•	Can handle egg-based custards more faithfully, without graininess.

⸻

👉 In short:
The Creami excels at small-batch, on-demand, unconventional frozen desserts, especially when your base would otherwise freeze too hard or too slushy in a churn. The compressor churn excels at classic creamy ice creams and gelatos, with smoother body and more professional texture for traditional recipes.

⸻
